l4_steps.name: Benchmark competitor in-flight service offerings
l4_steps.input: Annual CX strategy review cycle; competitor product reports
l4_steps.output: Competitive benchmarking report with service gap analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Benchmark coverage ≥10 direct competitors; report issued within 15 working days of cycle start
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data lacks cabin-class service detail; manual research from APEX/IFSA industry reports required, creating a 2–3 week lag in intelligence

l4_steps.name: Define cabin class service standards & sequences
l4_steps.input: Benchmarking report; brand guidelines; route profitability data from Amadeus SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Draft cabin class service standard document (Economy / Premium Economy / Business)
l4_steps.kpi: Standards documented for 100% of cabin classes within 20 working days
l4_steps.pain_point: No dedicated service-design tooling — standards authored in Confluence with no version-controlled approval workflow, leading to unapproved drafts reaching crew training

l4_steps.name: Obtain CX board approval for service standards
l4_steps.output: Approved service standard; ServiceNow change record CR raised
l4_steps.kpi: Board approval cycle ≤10 working days; zero unapproved standards in production
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-stakeholder approval (Inflight, Safety, Commercial, Legal) causes average 18-day delay; no SLA enforcement in ServiceNow CAB workflow

l4_steps.name: Publish service sequence manual to crew portal
l4_steps.input: Approved service standard; effective date from change record
l4_steps.output: Published service sequence manual version-controlled in FliteDeck; crew acknowledgement tracked
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active cabin crew acknowledge new manual within 5 days of publication
l4_steps.pain_point: FliteDeck acknowledgement tracking is available for pilot documents but EFB access for cabin crew varies by aircraft type, requiring parallel paper distribution on older fleets

l4_steps.name: Design seasonal menu & beverage programme
l4_steps.input: Approved service standards; route network data; passenger dietary preference trends from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Seasonal menu specification including SPML codes, allergen declarations, and portion specs
l4_steps.kpi: Menu refresh cycle ≤90 days; SPML coverage ≥18 dietary codes per IATA standard
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS SPML data completeness averages 62% — many passengers select meal preferences at airport rather than booking, causing last-minute galley shortfalls on long-haul sectors

l4_steps.name: Issue catering RFQ and evaluate supplier bids
l4_steps.input: Menu specification; volume forecasts from Amadeus SkyCAST; existing supplier contracts
l4_steps.output: Evaluated supplier shortlist; price per meal unit by route tier
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ response rate ≥80%; bid evaluation completed within 15 working days
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Ariba supplier onboarding for new catering vendors averages 30 days due to food safety certification upload requirements; limits ability to switch suppliers for disrupted routes

l4_steps.name: Validate food safety and regulatory compliance
l4_steps.input: Supplier bid documentation; HACCP plans; country-specific import/export food regulations
l4_steps.output: Compliance sign-off or rejection notice per supplier; allergen matrix approved
l4_steps.kpi: Zero non-compliant meals reaching aircraft; compliance review completed ≤10 working days
l4_steps.pain_point: Vary-by-country food import regulations (e.g. USDA restrictions, EU novel food rules) cause compliance hold-ups averaging 8 days per new ingredient, delaying menu finalisation

l4_steps.name: Finalise catering contracts and upload load plans
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba (Contract Management) + Gate Gourmet CateringIT Portal
l4_steps.output: Signed catering contract; galley load plans uploaded to Gate Gourmet CateringIT for route-level quantities
l4_steps.kpi: Contract executed ≥21 days before menu effective date; load plan accuracy ≥98% vs actual uplift
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate Gourmet CateringIT portal API integration with Amadeus Altéa PSS pax counts is batch-based (T-24h), not real-time — load plans cannot adjust dynamically for last-minute booking surges

l4_steps.name: Build service delivery training curriculum
l4_steps.input: Approved service sequence manual; new menu specifications; regulatory safety requirements (EASA OPS / FAR Part 121)
l4_steps.output: eLearning modules and practical assessment criteria published in Cornerstone LMS
l4_steps.kpi: Curriculum published ≥14 days before crew training cohort start; ≥90% module completion rate per cohort
l4_steps.pain_point: Cornerstone LMS integration with Jeppesen crew rostering is one-way — training completion status does not auto-block scheduling of uncertified crew, requiring manual cross-checks

l4_steps.name: Deliver in-flight service standards training to crew
l4_steps.system: Cornerstone OnDemand (LMS) + Cabin Crew Training Simulator
l4_steps.input: Training curriculum; crew roster from Jeppesen Crew Management; physical mock-up galley
l4_steps.output: Training completion records per crew member; practical simulation scores
l4_steps.kpi: Training completion ≥95% of active crew 7 days before go-live; practical assessment pass rate ≥88%
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator availability is constrained by shared scheduling with safety/emergency training (SEP); service training often deferred to on-aircraft familiarisation flights, increasing variability

l4_steps.name: Conduct service readiness assessment and certify crew
l4_steps.system: Cornerstone OnDemand (Competency Records) + Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: Practical assessment scores; eLearning completion certificates
l4_steps.output: Certified crew competency record; Jeppesen crew qualification flag updated
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of operating crew certified before standard go-live; re-assessment cycle ≤5 days for failures
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual update of qualification flags in Jeppesen after Cornerstone certification creates a 24–48h lag; uncertified crew can be legally rostered during the gap if not caught by manual audit

l4_steps.name: Configure galley layout and equipment specifications
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (MRO & Configuration Management)
l4_steps.input: Approved service standards; aircraft type galley drawings; catering load plans
l4_steps.output: Galley configuration specification per aircraft registration; AMOS configuration record updated
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration records updated for 100% of affected fleet tails ≥10 days before service go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet heterogeneity (B737-800 vs B737 MAX 8 vs B737-700 galley volumes differ by 8–12%) means single load plan cannot be applied uniformly, requiring per-subfleet configuration variants

l4_steps.name: Load galley manifest into catering management system
l4_steps.input: Per-aircraft galley configuration specs; route schedule from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Route-level galley manifest uploaded; catering uplift order generated per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest upload completed ≥48h before first operated flight; uplift accuracy target ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus SkyWORKS schedule changes (re-routes, aircraft swaps) are not automatically propagated to Gate Gourmet CateringIT — manual re-upload required within 2h of change notification to avoid mismatched uplift

l4_steps.name: Validate IFE content load and seat configuration
l4_steps.system: Panasonic Avionics eX3 Content Management System
l4_steps.input: Seasonal IFE content schedule; safety video version from Comply365; aircraft tail IFE compatibility matrix
l4_steps.output: Approved content load confirmation per tail; IFE configuration sign-off in Panasonic CMS
l4_steps.kpi: IFE content load verified on 100% of IFE-equipped tails ≥5 days before service period; zero safety video version mismatches
l4_steps.pain_point: Panasonic eX3 content load requires physical ground time per aircraft and cannot be pushed OTA to older eX1 installations; schedule compression means some tails miss the update window and carry previous season content

l4_steps.name: Execute in-flight service per approved standard
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen FliteDeck (Service Brief) + Gate Gourmet CateringIT (Manifest)
l4_steps.input: Published service sequence manual; galley manifest; pre-flight passenger count from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Completed in-flight service; wastage and shortfall log recorded on paper/EFB
l4_steps.kpi: Service sequence adherence ≥95% per audited flights; galley shortfall rate <2% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: No real-time digital cabin service tracking — adherence is measured through periodic audits only (sample <5% of flights), creating a large blind spot between audit cycles

l4_steps.name: Capture post-flight NPS and CSAT feedback
l4_steps.input: Completed flight; passenger email list from Amadeus Altéa PSS; post-flight survey trigger
l4_steps.output: NPS score and verbatim feedback per flight/route segment in Medallia dashboard
l4_steps.kpi: Survey response rate ≥18%; NPS target ≥45 for short-haul; ≥55 for long-haul
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS email suppression rules (opt-out, GDPR, corporate booking via Sabre GDS without passenger email) reduce survey reach by ~35%, skewing NPS samples toward direct-channel passengers

l4_steps.name: Analyse service performance metrics and complaints
l4_steps.system: Power BI (Connected to Medallia + ServiceNow + Altéa Data Warehouse)
l4_steps.input: Medallia NPS/CSAT data; ServiceNow complaint tickets; galley shortfall logs; audit scores
l4_steps.output: Monthly in-flight service performance dashboard; top 5 issue categories ranked by frequency and NPS impact
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published within 5 working days of month-end; complaint resolution rate ≥90% within SLA
l4_steps.pain_point: Medallia, ServiceNow, and Altéa data are held in separate systems with no automated ETL pipeline; Power BI refresh depends on manual CSV exports from Medallia, introducing 2–3 day data staleness

l4_steps.name: Identify root cause and implement service improvements
l4_steps.input: Performance dashboard; root cause analysis report; benchmarking data
l4_steps.output: Approved service improvement change record; updated service standard version in Confluence; re-entry to Step 1.2 if standard revision required
l4_steps.kpi: Root cause identified within 10 working days of threshold breach; improvement implemented within 30 days of approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Continuous improvement cycle lacks a formal feedback loop into Cornerstone LMS — identified training gaps require manual curriculum update requests, averaging 6-week lag before crew retraining is delivered
